role: Tests RespirationAnalyzer.estimateRespirationRate (RR-derived respiration via resample → Hann → DFT → 0.15-0.5 Hz peak): minimum sample count, known 15/12 br/min modulations, out-of-band inputs, constant and very short series.

units.does: Asserts 59 constant RR samples return nil (<60 guard).
units.entry: XCTest runner: test method on an XCTestCase subclass

units.does: Calls estimateRespirationRate on 60 constant samples and discards the result; asserts nothing.

flags.text: No assertion: the test only checks it does not crash; any return value, including a wrong rate, passes.

units.does: Feeds 300 RR values with 0.05 Hz modulation and asserts that if a rate is returned it is >= 6 br/min.
units.entry: XCTest runner: test method on an XCTestCase subclass

branches.effect: asserts rate >= 6; nil passes with no assertion

flags.text: Assertion cannot fail: respiratoryPeakFrequency only searches 0.15-0.5 Hz (9-30 br/min) and a final guard rejects <6, so any returned rate is >=9; a nil result also passes. The test does not pin that slow modulation is rejected.

The test is named 'RejectsImplausiblyLowRate' but the estimator does not reject it: a line-by-line Python replica of estimateRespirationRate (resample at 4 Hz, Hann DENORM, DFT, band 0.15-0.5 Hz) on this exact input returns 8.906 br/min (the band's lowest bin, Int(0.15/freqRes)=19 at freqRes 4/512), so a 3 br/min modulation is reported as a plausible ~9 br/min respiration rate and the test passes. There is no in-band power-ratio check (RespirationAnalysis.swift:76-87), so leakage from any out-of-band signal yields a band-edge rate.

units.does: Feeds 300 RR values with 0.8 Hz modulation and asserts that if a rate is returned it is <= 40 br/min.
units.entry: XCTest runner: test method on an XCTestCase subclass

branches.effect: asserts rate <= 40; nil passes with no assertion

flags.text: Assertion cannot fail: the band search caps the peak at 0.5 Hz (30 br/min) and a guard rejects >40, so the conditional assert is tautological; nil also passes.

With one RR per 0.8 s the 0.8 Hz modulation is above the beat-sampling Nyquist (0.625 Hz) and aliases; a Python replica of the estimator on this input returns 26.95 br/min, a plausible in-band rate, which the conditional <=40 assertion accepts. The test does not check rejection of high-rate input.
